source_text: Ταῦτα δὲ εἶπεν Ἡσαΐας, ὅτε εἶδε τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ, τουτέστι τοῦ Υἱοῦ· ὥστε καὶ Κύριος Σαβαώθ ἐστιν ὁ Υἱός. Κύριος γὰρ τῶν δυνάμεων ἑρμηνεύεται τὸ Κύριος Σαβαώθ· Ὁ δὲ Κύριος τῶν δυνάμεων, αὐτός ἐστιν ὁ βασιλεὺς τῆς δόξης, ὡς ὁ Δαβὶδ εἶπε· Κύριος δὲ τῆς δόξης ἐστὶν ὁ ἐσταυρωμένος Χριστὸς κατὰ τὸν Παῦλον. Καὶ καθὼς εἶπε Δαβίδ· Κύριος ποιμαίνει με, καὶ οὐδέν με ὑστερήσει· καὶ ἀλλαχοῦ· Ὁ ποιμαίνων τὸν Ἰσραὴλ, πρόσχες, ὁ ὁδηγῶν ὡσεὶ πρόβατον τὸν Ἰωσὴφ, ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τῶν χερουβὶμ, ἐμφάνηθι. Ἐν δὲ τοῖς Εὐαγγελίοις λέγει ὁ Υἱός· Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ποιμὴν ὁ καλός· αὐτὸς οὖν ἐστιν ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τῶν χερουβὶμ, ὁ ποιμαίνων τὸν Ἰσραήλ. Ὁ δὲ Παῦλος ἐν ταῖς Πράξεσι τὸ ἅγιον Πνεῦμα λέγει διὰ Ἡσαΐου εἰρηκέναι ταῦτα, ἅπερεἶπεν Ἡσαΐας, ὅτι Κύριος Σαβαώθ μοι εἶπεν. Ὁ Πατὴρ οὖν καὶ ὁ Υἱὸς καὶ τὸ ἅγιον Πνεῦμα Κύριος Σαβαώθ ἐστι. Καὶ ὅτε λέγει ἡ Γραφὴ περὶ τοῦ Πατρὸς, ὅτι Αὐτὸς ἔκτισε τὰ πάντα, τὰ ὁρατὰ καὶ τὰ ἀόρατα· ἀλλαχοῦ ἡ Γραφὴ διδάσκει ἡμᾶς, ὅτι διὰ τοῦ Υἱοῦ ἐκτίσθη. Οὐχ ἕτερα χωρὶς ὁ Πατὴρ ἔκτισε, καὶ ἄλλα ὁ Υἱός· ἀλλ' ἅπερ ὁ Πατὴρ ποιεῖ, διὰ τῆς ἰδίας δυνάμεως ποιεῖ, ἥτις ἐστὶν ὁ Υἱός· τὰ πάντα γὰρ δι' αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο. Οὕτως οὖν καὶ ὅτε λέγει ὁ Υἱός· Λύσατε τὸν ναὸν τοῦτον, καὶ ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις ἐγερῶ αὐτόν· ἔλεγε δὲ, φησὶ, περὶ τοῦ ἰδίου σώματος· ἑτέρα Γραφὴ λέγει, ὅτι Ὁ Πατὴρ ἤγειρε τὸν Υἱὸν αὐτοῦ ἐκ νεκρῶν· καὶ καλῶς λέγει· ἤγειρε γὰρ διὰ τοῦ ἰδίου Λόγου καὶ Υἱοῦ τὴν σάρκα 1004 τοῦ Υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ. Καὶ οὐ λέγομεν τὸ σῶμα εἶναι Υἱὸν φύσει τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἀλλὰ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ. Τοῦ οὖν σώματος ἐγειρομένου, ὁ Υἱὸς νοεῖται ἐγηγερμένος ἐκ νεκρῶν. Διὰ τοῦτο κατὰ σάρκα λέγομεν, ὅτι καὶ ἀπέθανε, καὶ ἐτάφη, καὶ ἠγέρθη ἐκ νεκρῶν· κατὰ δὲ τὸ πνεῦμα καὶ ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς ἦν καὶ πανταχοῦ. Ἐπεὶ οὖν πρότερον πλούσιος ὢν, τουτέστι Θεός· ὕστερον δὲ πτωχὸς γέγονε, τουτέστιν ἄνθρωπος, καὶ ὡμοιώθη ἡμῖν κατὰ πάντα χωρὶς ἁμαρτίας· καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ὡς ἄνθρωπος λαμβάνει ζωὴν, ὁ ἔχων ζωὴν, αὐτὸς γάρ ἐστιν ἡ ζωή· λαμβάνει δὲ δι' ἡμᾶς, καὶ ὡς ἄνθρωπος προέκοπτε σοφίᾳ καὶ ἡλικίᾳ ἡ ἀΐδιος τοῦ Θεοῦ δύναμις καὶ σοφία, καὶ ὡς ἄνθρωπος ἁγιάζεται ὁ ἅγιος, καὶ μὴ χρείαν ἔχων ἁγιασμοῦ· Ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν γὰρ, φησὶν, ἁγιάζω ἐμαυτὸν, ἵνα ὦσιν αὐτοὶ ἡγιασμένοι ἐν ἀληθείᾳ. Καὶ ὡς ἄνθρωπος ὑψοῦται λαβὼν ὄνομα τὸ ὑπὲρ πᾶν ὄνομα, ὅπερ ἀεὶ κατὰ φύσιν ἔχει. Θεὸς γὰρ ἦν, φησὶν, ὁ Λόγος. Ὅσα οὖν λέγει ἡ Γραφὴ ὅτι ἔλαβεν ὁ Υἱὸς, διὰ τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ λέγει, ὅπερ σῶμα ἀπαρχή ἐστι τῆς Ἐκκλησίας· Ἀπαρχὴ γὰρ, φησὶν, ὁ Χριστός. Τῆς οὖν ἀπαρχῆς λαβούσης ὄνομα τὸ ὑπὲρ πᾶν ὄνομα, συνηγέρθη δυνάμει καὶ τὸ φύραμα, καὶ συνεκαθέσθη, κατὰ τὸ λεγόμενον· Καὶ συνήγειρε καὶ συνεκάθισε.
thought_title: The Son is Lord of hosts, and the Father acts through him
orientation: Marcellus is arguing that the Son is the Lord of hosts whom Isaiah saw, and that the Father does all things through the Son, including raising and sanctifying the Son's own flesh.
pass_a_gloss: And Isaiah said these things when he saw his glory, that is, of the Son; so that the Son is also Lord of hosts. For Lord of hosts is interpreted Lord of powers. And the Lord of powers, he is the king of glory, as David said. And the Lord of glory is the crucified Christ according to Paul. And as David said: The Lord shepherds me, and nothing will be lacking to me; and elsewhere: O shepherd of Israel, give heed, O guide of Joseph like a sheep, O you who sit upon the cherubim, appear. And in the Gospels the Son says: I am the good shepherd; he therefore is the one who sits upon the cherubim, the one who shepherds Israel. And Paul in Acts says that the Holy Spirit said these things through Isaiah, which Isaiah said, that the Lord of hosts said to me. Therefore the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit is Lord of hosts. And when the Scripture says about the Father, that he created all things, the visible and the invisible; elsewhere the Scripture teaches us, that through the Son they were created. Not different things did the Father create apart, and other things the Son; but what the Father does, he does through his own power, which is the Son; for all things came to be through him. So therefore also when the Son says: Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it; and he was speaking, it says, about his own body; another Scripture says, that the Father raised his Son from the dead; and it says well; for he raised through his own Word and Son the flesh 1004 of his Son. And we do not say that the body is Son by nature of God, but the body of the Son of God. Therefore when the body is raised, the Son is understood to have been raised from the dead. Because of this according to the flesh we say, that he both died, and was buried, and was raised from the dead; but according to the spirit he was both in heaven and on earth and everywhere. Since therefore being rich before, that is, God; and later he became poor, that is, man, and he was made like us in all things apart from sin; and because of this as man he receives life, the one who has life, for he himself is the life; and he receives it for us, and as man the eternal power and wisdom of God advanced in wisdom and stature, and as man the holy one is sanctified, though having no need of sanctification; For on their behalf, it says, I sanctify myself, that they themselves may be sanctified in truth. And as man he is exalted, having received the name above every name, which he always has by nature. For God, it says, was the Word. Therefore whatever the Scripture says that the Son received, it says because of his body, which body is the firstfruits of the Church; For the firstfruits, it says, is Christ. Therefore when the firstfruits received the name above every name, the lump was also raised together in power, and was seated together, according to what is said: And he raised together and seated together.

choices.why: Fixed glossary rendering for the divine title, applied here to Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.
Glossary term for the Son's voluntary lowliness in becoming human; kept as 'poor' to preserve the contrast with 'rich' (God).
Fixed glossary rendering for Christ's body as the first portion of the Church.
Glossary term for the incarnate human nature of the Son; kept as 'flesh' rather than 'body' to distinguish from σῶμα.

choices.term: ὁμοιώθη ἡμῖν κατὰ πάντα χωρὶς ἁμαρτίας
choices.english: he was made like us in all things apart from sin
choices.why: Preserves the passive force of ὁμοιώθη and the exact scope of the likeness.
rejected: he became like us in every way except sin

choices.why: Keeps the Pauline image of the dough from Romans 11:16, where the firstfruits sanctify the whole lump.

pass_b_english: Isaiah said these things when he saw his glory—that is, the glory of the Son. So the Son is also Lord of hosts. For “Lord of hosts” means “Lord of the powers.” And the Lord of the powers is himself the King of glory, as David said. And the Lord of glory is the crucified Christ, according to Paul. And as David said: “The Lord shepherds me, and nothing will be lacking to me” (Psalm 23:1). And elsewhere: “O Shepherd of Israel, give heed, you who lead Joseph like a flock, you who sit upon the cherubim, appear” (Psalm 80:1). In the Gospels the Son says: “I am the good shepherd” (John 10:11). So he himself is the one who sits upon the cherubim, the Shepherd of Israel.

Paul says in Acts that the Holy Spirit said through Isaiah the very things Isaiah said, that the Lord of hosts said to me. So the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit are Lord of hosts. And when Scripture says about the Father that he created all things, visible and invisible, elsewhere Scripture teaches us that they were created through the Son. The Father did not create some things separately and the Son other things. Rather, whatever the Father does, he does through his own power, which is the Son. For “all things came into being through him” (John 1:3).

So also when the Son says: “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up”—and he was speaking, it says, about his own body—another Scripture says that the Father raised his Son from the dead. And it says this rightly. For he raised the flesh of his Son through his own Word and Son. And we do not say that the body is by nature the Son of God, but that it is the body of the Son of God. So when the body is raised, the Son is understood to have been raised from the dead.

For this reason we say that according to the flesh he died, and was buried, and was raised from the dead. But according to the Spirit he was in heaven and on earth and everywhere. Since he was first rich—that is, God—and afterward became poor—that is, man—and was made like us in all things apart from sin, for this reason as man he receives life, he who has life, for he himself is the life. He receives it for our sake. And as man the eternal power and wisdom of God advanced in wisdom and stature. And as man he is sanctified, he who is holy and has no need of sanctification. For he says: “For their sake I sanctify myself, so that they also may be sanctified in truth” (John 17:19). And as man he is exalted, receiving the name that is above every name, which he always possesses by nature. For “the Word was God” (John 1:1).

So whatever Scripture says the Son received, it says because of his body, which body is the firstfruits of the Church. For “Christ is the firstfruits” (1 Corinthians 15:20). So when the firstfruits received the name that is above every name, the lump was also raised with him by power and seated together with him, according to what is said: “And he raised us together and seated us together” (Ephesians 2:6).
notes: The number 1004 appears in the source text after σάρκα; it is likely a page or column number from the manuscript and not part of the text.

problems.quote: the lump was also raised together with him in power and seated together with him
problems.source_quote: συνηγέρθη δυνάμει καὶ τὸ φύραμα, καὶ συνεκαθέσθη
problems.why: English misplaces 'in power': δυνάμει goes with συνηγέρθη ('was raised by/in power'), not modifying 'the lump was raised.' The lump is raised by power, not 'in power' as an adverbial modifier of the lump's state.
problems.fix: the lump was also raised with him by power and seated together with him

problems.source_quote: Ὁ ποιμαίνων τὸν Ἰσραὴλ, πρόσχες, ὁ ὁδηγῶν ὡσεὶ πρόβατον τὸν Ἰωσὴφ, ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τῶν χερουβὶμ, ἐμφάνηθι
problems.why: LXX Psalm 79:1, not 80:1 in Hebrew/English numbering.
problems.ruling: LXX Psalm 79:1 matches the Greek; English 'Psalm 80:1' uses Hebrew numbering, misleading readers of the LXX citation.

edits.old: the lump was also raised together with him in power and seated together with him
edits.new: the lump was also raised with him by power and seated together with him

fixed: Corrected 'in power' to 'by power' to reflect δυνάμει as the means by which the lump was raised.
Corrected Psalm reference from 80:1 to 79:1 per Hebrew/English numbering of LXX Psalm 79.

problems.quote: because “the Lord of hosts said to me.”
problems.why: Source has διότι ('because') explaining why Spirit said through Isaiah; 'said to me' should be 'said these things' (ταῦτα).
problems.fix: that the Lord of hosts said these things.
problems.ruling: Source ὅτι introduces quotation, not 'because'; μοι εἶπεν is 'said to me,' but context requires ταῦτα (these things) from earlier clause.

problems.source_quote: Ὁ ποιμαίνων τὸν Ἰσραὴλ, πρόσχες, ὁ ὁδηγῶν ὡσεὶ πρόβατον τὸν Ἰωσὴφ, ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τῶν χερουβὶμ, ἐμφάνηθι
problems.why: This is Psalm 80:1 (Hebrew/English), not Psalm 79:1. LXX Psalm 79 = Hebrew Psalm 80.
problems.ruling: LXX Psalm 79 = Hebrew/English Psalm 80; citing '79:1' misleads readers familiar with English Bibles.

edits.old: because “the Lord of hosts said to me.”
edits.new: that the Lord of hosts said these things.

fixed: Changed 'because “the Lord of hosts said to me.”' to 'that the Lord of hosts said these things.' The source has ταῦτα ('these things'), not 'to me', and the clause is introduced by ὅτι, which here introduces the content of what the Spirit said, not a causal 'because'.
Changed 'Psalm 79:1' to 'Psalm 80:1'. The source quotes LXX Psalm 79, which corresponds to Hebrew/English Psalm 80.

problems.quote: Paul says in Acts that the Holy Spirit said through Isaiah
problems.source_quote: Ὁ δὲ Παῦλος ἐν ταῖς Πράξεσι τὸ ἅγιον Πνεῦμα λέγει διὰ Ἡσαΐου εἰρηκέναι ταῦτα, ἅπερ εἶπεν Ἡσαΐας, ὅτι Κύριος Σαβαώθ μοι εἶπεν
problems.why: English omits "ὅτι Κύριος Σαβαώθ μοι εἶπεν" (that the Lord of hosts said to me), crucial for the argument.
problems.fix: Paul says in Acts that the Holy Spirit said through Isaiah the very things Isaiah said, that the Lord of hosts said to me.

problems.quote: And as man the eternal power and wisdom of God advanced in wisdom and stature.
problems.source_quote: καὶ ὡς ἄνθρωπος προέκοπτε σοφίᾳ καὶ ἡλικίᾳ ἡ ἀΐδιος τοῦ Θεοῦ δύναμις καὶ σοφία
problems.why: Source says the eternal power and wisdom of God progressed as man; English makes 'as man' modify only the advancing, losing the subject identification.
problems.fix: And as man the eternal power and wisdom of God advanced in wisdom and stature.
problems.ruling: Greek: 'ὡς ἄνθρωπος...ἡ ἀΐδιος...δύναμις καὶ σοφία' = 'as man...the eternal power and wisdom'; English wrongly makes 'as man' only modify the participle, not the subject.

edits.old: Paul says in Acts that the Holy Spirit said through Isaiah the very things Isaiah said, that the Lord of hosts said these things.
edits.new: Paul says in Acts that the Holy Spirit said through Isaiah the very things Isaiah said, that the Lord of hosts said to me.

fixed: Added the omitted clause 'that the Lord of hosts said to me' (ὅτι Κύριος Σαβαώθ μοι εἶπεν), which the English had rendered as 'said these things' and thereby lost the first-person quotation crucial to the argument.
The sentence about the eternal power and wisdom of God advancing as man already renders the source accurately; no change needed.

last_rejected.why: ποιμαίνει means 'shepherds' but context demands 'is my shepherd' (Psalm 23:1)
last_rejected.ruling: ποιμαίνει means 'shepherds'; present active indicative is standard for Psalm 23:1 LXX.

last_rejected.quote: O Shepherd of Israel, give heed, you who lead Joseph like a flock
last_rejected.source_quote: Ὁ ποιμαίνων τὸν Ἰσραὴλ, πρόσχες, ὁ ὁδηγῶν ὡσεὶ πρόβατον τὸν Ἰωσήφ
last_rejected.why: ὁδηγῶν means 'guiding/leading' but 'lead...like a flock' misrepresents ὡσεὶ πρόβατον which modifies Joseph not the verb
last_rejected.fix: O Shepherd of Israel, give heed, you who guide Joseph like a sheep
last_rejected.ruling: ὁδηγῶν ὡσεὶ πρόβατον τὸν Ἰωσήφ = 'leading Joseph like a sheep/flock'; rendering is within normal range.

last_rejected.quote: Paul says in Acts that the Holy Spirit said through Isaiah
last_rejected.source_quote: Ὁ δὲ Παῦλος ἐν ταῖς Πράξεσι τὸ ἅγιον Πνεῦμα λέγει διὰ Ἡσαΐου εἰρηκέναι ταῦτα
last_rejected.why: English hides that Paul is the speaker citing the Spirit; 'Paul says...the Spirit said' makes Paul the subject of 'says' about the Spirit, but source has Paul saying the Spirit spoke
last_rejected.fix: Paul says in Acts that the Holy Spirit spoke through Isaiah
last_rejected.ruling: 'Paul says...the Holy Spirit said' correctly renders Παῦλος λέγει τὸ Πνεῦμα εἰρηκέναι; Paul is speaker.

last_rejected.quote: the lump was also raised with him by power
last_rejected.why: δυνάμει means 'in power' or 'powerfully' not 'by power' as instrumental agent; misrepresents how lump was raised
last_rejected.fix: the lump was also raised with him in power
last_rejected.ruling: δυνάμει with genitive can be instrumental 'by power'; standard rendering, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: And he raised us together and seated us together
last_rejected.why: Missing object 'us' in the Greek quote; English adds 'us' making it a complete citation but source has abbreviated quotation without explicit object
last_rejected.fix: And raised together and seated together
last_rejected.ruling: συνήγειρε καὶ συνεκάθισε implies 'us' from Eph 2:6 context; adding object for English clarity is normal.
